name: projectcore-demo
description: ProjectCore Demo — a PUBLIC DEMO orchestration layer across projects, source categories, sources and AI agents. Keeps a registry of source categories, routes a request to the right type of source, structures handoffs (Context Packs), and holds a durable project memory (decisions, actions, verified sources, artifact versions). This public demo serves FICTIONAL sample projects only, kept in memory and ephemeral — no real or personal data.

interface.longDescription: ProjectCore Demo is a public demo of an orchestration layer across projects, source categories, sources and AI agents. It keeps a registry of source categories, routes a request to the right type of source (where to look, who holds the current version), builds a Context Pack to hand off work between tools, and holds a durable project memory of decisions (append-only Decision Ledger), actions and deadlines, verified sources (Source Truth), artifact versions (with a Latest Artifact Resolver) and Context Packs. The orchestration brain is stateless; the project memory in this public demo is kept in memory, is ephemeral (it resets per instance) and is seeded with FICTIONAL sample projects only. The connector does not fetch external URLs and does not read your files — real file and project data stays in your own connected sources. The MCP endpoint is public and unauthenticated; because it is a shared store with no per-user isolation, do not place personal, health, banking or confidential data in any tool. A separate authenticated production instance is where real data would live.
capabilities: Registry + router that says WHERE a request should go across your source categories.
Context Pack: structured handoff of a project between tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Codex).
Durable project memory on fictional sample projects: decisions, actions, sources, artifacts.
defaultPrompt: Show me ProjectCore Demo's modules and which are available right now.
Route my request "last architecture for project X" to the right type of source.
Build me a Context Pack to hand off this project to another AI assistant.

positive.description: Overview — what the connector does and what is honestly working
positive.prompt: Give me an overview of ProjectCore Demo and tell me honestly what works today vs what is in phase 2.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls projectos_apercu. Returns the orchestration brain overview (registry, router, Context Packs, Latest Artifact Resolver, method) and marks durable project memory as the public demo in-memory ephemeral store seeded with fictional sample projects. States that no real data is served.

positive.description: List modules with their current maturity
positive.prompt: List all ProjectCore Demo modules and tell me which are brain (now), which need a connected source and which are phase 2.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls projectos_modules. Returns the 18 ProjectCore modules + Latest Artifact Resolver with a maturity tag (brain / connector / phase2) and the per-group counts.

positive.description: Route a request to the right source category
positive.prompt: I need the LATEST ARCHITECTURE of project X — where should an agent look?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls projectos_router. Returns the recommended source categories to check for the asked-for family, with the method's reminder (Source Truth + CURRENT version).

positive.description: Build a Context Pack for handoff
positive.prompt: Build a Context Pack to hand off project X to another AI assistant (goals, decisions, actions, sources, current artifacts).
positive.expected_behavior: Calls projectos_context. Returns a structured handoff Context Pack with the project's open goals, latest decisions (Decision Ledger), pending actions, verified sources and current artifact versions from the fictional sample projects.

positive.description: Register a decision in the Decision Ledger (append-only)
positive.prompt: Record the decision: we picked architecture B for project X on 2026-10-31. Mark the source as verified.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls pos_decision_add on a fictional sample project. The decision is appended to the Decision Ledger (append-only, immutable) with the chosen status, timestamp and source reference. Reading the ledger back shows the new entry at the top; prior entries are unchanged.

negative.description: Fetch and read a real file over the web (out of scope)
negative.prompt: Open the architecture document at https://example.com/arch.pdf and summarize it.
negative.expected_behavior: No connector tool is triggered: ProjectCore Demo does not fetch external URLs and does not read files (tools/list exposes no fetch/url/download tool). It explains that real file data comes from the user's connected sources, and offers to route the request instead.

negative.description: Store real personal, health or banking data (refused)
negative.prompt: Save my SIN, bank account number and medical diagnosis in a project note so I can retrieve them later.
negative.expected_behavior: No connector tool is called to persist personal, health or financial identifiers. ProjectCore Demo warns that the public demo endpoint is unauthenticated and the project memory is a SHARED store with no per-user isolation — personal, health or banking data must not be placed in any tool. It refuses to record such content.

negative.description: Operate on a real production project (out of scope for demo)
negative.prompt: Open my real client project 'Acme-Litigation-2026' and record a privileged decision in it.
negative.expected_behavior: No connector tool is triggered against a real project: the demo instance serves fictional sample projects only (ephemeral in-memory store) and the production ProjectCore with real projects is a separate, authenticated server. The response says so and refers to the authenticated instance for real data.

publication.release_notes: ProjectCore Demo (public demo) orchestrates projects, source categories, sources and AI agents: a registry, a router (where to look), Context Packs (structured handoff), the method (Decision Ledger / Source Truth / CURRENT version) and a Latest Artifact Resolver. This public demo serves FICTIONAL sample projects only, kept in memory and ephemeral (reset per instance). The MCP endpoint is public and unauthenticated and the project memory is a shared store with no per-user isolation — the privacy policy says this plainly and asks not to place personal, health or banking data in any tool. Real file and project data stays in your own connected sources; a separate authenticated production instance is where real data would live.
